title: Add tiered batching dashboards + canary alert rules (latency / queue delay / batch formation)
author: Felix Schneider
commits: dashboards: add Tiered Batching Overview with variables for tier/model/region
dashboards: add Latency by tier (p50/p95/p99 + regression panel vs baseline window)
dashboards: add Queue delay + batch formation breakdown (size, wait, formation rate)
alerts: add canary-focused alert rules (p95 latency regression, queue delay, timeouts)
docs: update README with import paths + required labels/metrics
body:
## Summary
Adds Grafana dashboard JSON definitions and Prometheus alert rules for monitoring tiered batching (fast / standard / cost_efficient) during perf canary runs and staged rollouts.

This PR is intended to support the Workload-aware batching defaults beta rollout by giving SRE/on-call a single place to validate that:
- latency SLOs are holding per tier (p50/p95/p99)
- queue delay and batch wait time are within guardrails
- batch formation is behaving as expected (batch size distributions, formation rate)
- regressions can be detected quickly during canary ramp (alerts tuned for signal > noise)

## Dashboards added
1) **Tiered Batching: Overview**
- Topline: request rate, error rate, timeout/cancel rate, GPU utilization
- Latency by tier + route (chat/completions/embeddings) with model + region slices
- "Effective tier coverage" panel: percent of traffic with `batching_tier` label present (helps catch missing labels during partial rollouts)

2) **Tiered Batching: Latency & Streaming Health**
- p50/p95/p99 request latency by `batching_tier`, `model`, `region`, `deployment_mode`
- Streaming cadence proxy panels (where available): time-to-first-token and per-token interval histograms
- Tail latency drilldown: p99 latency correlated with queue delay p99 and batch wait p99

3) **Tiered Batching: Queue Delay & Batch Formation**
- Queue delay histograms + p95/p99 by tier
- Batch size distributions (prefill and decode where exposed)
- Batch formation rate and batch wait time (helps detect over-batching or under-batching)
- Admission/load shedding overlays: shed reason codes by tier (to validate cost_efficient tier interacts with overload protection correctly)

4) **Tiered Batching: Canary Comparison**
- Designed for perf-canary jobs and staged ramp
- Panels compare current 30m window vs previous 24h baseline (same region/model) using Grafana transformations
- Explicit callouts for "fast tier streaming regression" signatures (queue delay low but p95 high + elevated time-to-first-token)

## Alerts added (canary monitoring)
All alert rules are namespaced under `tiered_batching_canary/*` and default to **warning** severity. These are intended to page only when combined with rollout playbook signals (see ENG-18427 checklist); we are keeping them non-paging by default to avoid noisy alerts from short-lived canary spikes.

New rules (high level):
- `tiered_batching_canary_p95_latency_regression`:
  - triggers when p95 latency for a tier/model/region is > **15%** above baseline for 15m (requires minimum request volume)
- `tiered_batching_canary_queue_delay_p99_high`:
  - triggers when queue delay p99 exceeds tier guardrail thresholds (fast < 15ms, standard < 40ms, cost_efficient < 90ms) for 10m
- `tiered_batching_canary_timeout_rate_high`:
  - triggers when timeout rate > 0.8% for 10m and rising
- `tiered_batching_canary_cancel_rate_spike`:
  - triggers on cancellation spikes (often indicates client impatience due to cadence/latency regression)
- `tiered_batching_canary_label_coverage_missing`:
  - triggers when > 5% of traffic lacks `batching_tier` label during an enabled rollout (catches misconfigured exporters or partial rollout paths)

## Metrics / labels expected
These dashboards assume the runtime + gateway exporters emit (names as used in current dashboards):
- `redwood_inference_request_latency_ms_bucket` (labels include: `route`, `model`, `region`, `deployment_mode`, `batching_tier`)
- `redwood_scheduler_queue_delay_ms_bucket` (same label set as above)
- `redwood_batch_size` (histogram or summary depending on env; dashboards support both patterns)
- `redwood_batch_wait_ms_bucket`
- `redwood_request_timeouts_total`, `redwood_request_canceled_total`
- `redwood_overload_shed_total` (label `reason`)

If `batching_tier` label is missing, panels will still render but will collapse into "unknown"; alert `label_coverage_missing` is meant to catch this early.

## Files changed
- `dashboards/tiered-batching/overview.json`
- `dashboards/tiered-batching/latency-streaming.json`
- `dashboards/tiered-batching/queue-delay-batch-formation.json`
- `dashboards/tiered-batching/canary-comparison.json`
- `alerts/tiered-batching-canary.rules.yaml`
- `alerts/README.md`
- `dashboards/README.md`
- `dashboards/_shared/variables.libsonnet`
- `dashboards/_shared/panels/latency.libsonnet`

## Notable implementation details
- All dashboards use a consistent variable set: `env`, `cluster`, `region`, `deployment_mode`, `route`, `model`, `gpu_sku`, `batching_tier`.
- Aggregations default to `sum by (le, ...)` for buckets and `histogram_quantile()` for pXX.
- Canary comparison dashboard uses a baseline query pattern that is stable for low/medium traffic (requires `min_requests` guard). This avoids a bunch of false positives during beta cohort ramp.

## Test plan
- Imported dashboards into staging Grafana (`staging-us-east1`) and verified panels populate for perf-canary run ID `pcan-2025-03-22T18:40Z`.
- Verified alert rules load via `promtool check rules` in CI.
- Manually forced a regression scenario by filtering to a known-degraded run (queue delay spike) and confirmed panels/threshold coloring.

## Follow-ups
- Once runtime PRs land everywhere, we should confirm `gpu_sku` label cardinality is bounded in prod (we currently filter to known SKUs in variables).
- Threshold tuning: queue delay p99 thresholds may need minor adjustment after the first week of beta (SRE thread notes suggest fast-tier noise under extremely low QPS).
conversation:
Aisha Bello (review): The canary rules look reasonable, but I’m worried `queue_delay_p99_high` will flap on low traffic. Can we add a minimum QPS guard similar to the latency regression rule?
Felix Schneider (author): Good call. Added `min_over_time(rate(redwood_inference_requests_total[5m])) > 2` gate per series; also reduced the evaluation window from 15m -> 10m to keep it responsive.

Allison Grant (review): Please align tier guardrails with the SLO tier doc wording (fast/standard/cost_efficient). Also the label key is `batching_tier` in runtime PRs, but this dashboard variable uses `tier` in a couple places.
Felix Schneider (author): Fixed the variable key to `batching_tier` everywhere and updated legend strings to match naming. I also added a note to the dashboard README about expected labels.

Sergio Costa (review): Canary comparison dashboard is great. One request: add a panel for shed reasons by tier (cost_efficient especially) so on-call can distinguish overload protection from actual scheduler regression.
Felix Schneider (author): Added `redwood_overload_shed_total` stacked by `reason` with tier split and linked it to the queue delay drilldown.

Caleb Johnson (review): Any chance we can include trace exemplars on the tail latency panels?
Felix Schneider (author): Not in this PR (exemplars aren’t consistently enabled across all clusters). I added a placeholder link + TODO in the README; we can wire exemplars once the tracing ingestion config is uniform.

Sean Gallagher (review): Please confirm the guardrails match the current SRE thresholds. fast: 15ms queue delay p99, standard: 40ms, cost_efficient: 90ms is what we discussed. Also ensure these are warning-level only.
Felix Schneider (author): Confirmed thresholds and set all new alerts to warning severity with an explicit comment that paging policy is owned by SRE. (No routing changes in this repo.)

Final review: Aisha approved after QPS guard change. Allison approved after label fixes. Sergio approved after shed panel added.
release_notes: Adds tiered batching dashboards and canary alert rules for monitoring latency/queue delay/batch formation during rollout of workload-aware batching defaults.
